scope: Bounded evolution from fabricated contacts to exact Sharpa-pad smoke acceptance
summary: After five retained failures, the 33-frame v11 smoke passes actual mesh contact, nonnegative force closure, articulated topology, causal response, video, and all bundle-lineage gates.
evidence: v5 found zero exact contacts because the original wrist target was 8-10 cm from the fingertip pads.
v6 retained three contacts early but lost them under an unrealistically compressed short-rollout trajectory; v7 reached at least three fingertips and rank six but failed the positive wrench cone.

v8 showed that unconstrained least squares returned one negative-weight solution for redundant contact patches; v9 retained nonnegative weights but exposed floating 0.02 N comparisons and incomplete solver convergence.
v10 passes 15/15 exact-contact force-closure frames after a probability-simplex nonnegative solver and numerical tolerance fix.
v11 adds embedded FPS and passes every independent bundle manifest, hash, source, frame, timeline, coordinate, and stem-ID gate.
lessons: Reduced smoke motion must preserve physical speed rather than compressing a full-amplitude trajectory into 1.375 seconds.
Force closure for a distributed compliant patch requires a nonnegative convex solver; an unconstrained least-squares solution with negative coefficients cannot prove infeasibility.
limitations: The accepted artifact covers 33 simulated frames, not the required 660-frame timeline.
next_actions: Run the exact-pad contact mode over all 660 frames and reject unless every contact frame passes.
